requirements.requirement: Dedicated `inventorysvc` system account created on node1
requirements.summary: useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /sbin/nologin inventorysvc succeeded and id inventorysvc confirmed uid=995(inventorysvc), a dedicated non-login system account not present at baseline (baseline showed 'no such user').

requirements.requirement: /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker run as a managed service named `inventory-worker` on node1
requirements.summary: A systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service was created with ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker, enabled and started via systemctl enable --now; systemctl status confirmed active (running) with the correct ExecStart path.

requirements.requirement: Service process runs under the inventorysvc account
requirements.summary: Unit specifies User=inventorysvc/Group=inventorysvc; ps -o pid,user,cmd showed the running process (and its child sleep) owned by 'invento+' (inventorysvc).

requirements.requirement: Service is enabled to persist (start automatically) rather than only started ad hoc
requirements.summary: systemctl is-enabled inventory-worker returned 'enabled' both immediately after setup and again after a full node restart, with the service auto-starting and continuing to run as inventorysvc post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: (Provider-wide protocol, independent of task contract) Full restart evidence cycle for node1: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/account state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id d6298ced... and healthy active/enabled service captured (cmd-8eabb098e0054e92); systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged before disconnect (cmd-c4c6ed035d284a6b); node briefly unreachable then boot_id changed to ccf55dbd... with fresh uptime (cmd-91e8f76d30834a15, cmd-59d2c9ff21674844); post-restart inventory-worker confirmed active/enabled with new PID and process still owned by inventorysvc (cmd-c99b0f6b31c64f1d). This is corroborated by the fixed global boot-identity snapshots (after_prepare d6298ced... vs after_executor ccf55dbd...), which match the executor's own pre/post boot IDs exactly.

overall_summary: The executor fully satisfied the task contract: os-comparison-worker runs as the systemd-managed service inventory-worker under a newly created dedicated inventorysvc system account on node1, verified enabled/active with the correct process owner both immediately after setup and again after a full, directly observed node restart (changed boot_id, brief disconnect, recovered service state). The independent global boot-identity snapshots corroborate the executor's own before/after boot IDs. No unnecessary or unsafe mutations were found.
limitations: Restart evidence relies on a single reboot cycle observed only through boot_id/uptime and service status; no deeper data/cluster-state check was applicable since this is a single-node, stateless worker service.
One command (cmd-91e8f76d30834a15) returned a connection-reset error, but this is the expected transient disconnect during systemctl reboot, not a task failure.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map cleanly to task requirements or the mandated restart protocol: user creation, unit file creation, enable/start, baseline capture, reboot issuance, and post-reboot verification. No unrelated packages were installed, no failed/troubleshooting mutations appear in the timeline, and the global failed-services and package-health snapshots show no residue (empty failed-services list, dnf healthy before and after). The reboot produced a small, expected /tmp/reboot.log artifact from the executor's own redirect and new systemd-private ephemeral dirs tied to the fresh boot session -- both low-risk, non-destructive, and a normal byproduct of the required restart rather than an unnecessary mutation. Listening sockets changed only in sshd's PID (same ports), consistent with the reboot, not a new exposure.
